INTEGRATED SCIENCE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reproduction in plants.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Reproduction in plants.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reproduction in plants.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structure of the atom? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structure of the atom.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Structure of the atom.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structure of the atom.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.

3. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Milk souring
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Iron rusting

4. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

5. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Overgrazing continuously

6. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A mixture of two liquids

7. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Producers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Decomposers only

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Interdependence of Life? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Interdependence of Life.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on The Interdependence of Life.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Interdependence of Life.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water hardness? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water hardness.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water hardness.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Water hardness.

10. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. watt (W)
   C. newton (N)
   D. joule (J)

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Metals and Alloys? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Metals and Alloys.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Metals and Alloys.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Metals and Alloys.

12. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

13. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Glucose and oxygen

14. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 0 °C

15. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition in animals.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition in animals.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition in animals.

17. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Curved mirrors? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Curved mirrors.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Curved mirrors.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Curved mirrors.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
18. In three clear sentences, explain Structure of the atom and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Metals and Alloys and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Water hardness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Reproduction in plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain The Interdependence of Life and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Curved mirrors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Structure of the atom and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain Metals and Alloys and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

27. In three clear sentences, explain Water hardness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
